turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Pop him up on Mom's lap for me. Temperature's 101.6, heart rate 128, respirations 28, oxygen sat 97 percent, and blood pressure 96 over 60.
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Okay. He's been a little furnace since, um, whenever this started.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, one sec, this thing just logged me out again. Alright. What's going on with him?
[SEG0004] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Fever and a cough. He's four. It came on after preschool, I think about a week.
[SEG0005] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It is not a week, Elena. Thursday night. Three days. I was the one home.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Say that timing once more? I was clicking the wrong chart.
[SEG0007] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The cough, about a week. He was stuffy before that, maybe, I don't know.
[SEG0008] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Cough and the fever both kicked off Thursday. Three days. Not a week.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): So somewhere between three days and a week, and you're not agreeing. I'll leave it there. How high did it get at home?
[SEG0010] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I got 102.
[SEG0011] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The forehead scanner said 104.2 last night. Hers is the old one.
[SEG0012] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That scanner runs hot. I did it under his arm and, well, actually I redid it under his tongue and it was 102.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, what was the number? 102 or 104?
[SEG0014] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): 104.2. Forehead scanner. I'm sticking with that.
[SEG0015] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And it was 102 in his mouth. I'm not calling it 104.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright, you two don't match. Jonah, hey buddy, does your throat hurt?
[SEG0017] person_5 (PATIENT): Throat hurts.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tummy? Ears?
[SEG0019] person_5 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0020] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He hasn't said his ears hurt and he's not pulling at them. No vomiting, no rash that I've seen.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any trouble breathing at home? Going fast, or any color change?
[SEG0022] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. He breathes fine. The cough just gets worse when he lies down, wakes him up.
[SEG0023] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yeah, nights are the bad part. Daytime he's whiny but okay.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): What did you give him for the fever?
[SEG0025] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The grape Tylenol, the kids' fever one. One teaspoon, the little plastic spoon in the box, every six hours.
[SEG0026] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That was not one spoon. It was two. And this morning I gave him the berry Motrin on top.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hang on, the screen jumped. Two spoons of which bottle?
[SEG0028] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Two spoons of the grape Tylenol. And one spoon of the berry Motrin, the ibuprofen, this morning. Maybe the spoon wasn't full, I kind of eyeballed it.
[SEG0029] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Tylenol was one teaspoon, filled to the line. You did give the Motrin, fine, one little spoon this morning. That's it.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay, so the Tylenol amount is still a fight, and the Motrin was one unmeasured spoon once. Anything else? Inhalers, cough medicine?
[SEG0031] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's got the purple inhaler, the albuterol, from when he wheezed. Two puffs at night the last couple nights, cough was all rattly.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): When did that wheezing start? When did they give you the inhaler?
[SEG0033] person_5 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0034] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Last winter, or the one before. I can't tell you which. They just handed us the purple one.
[SEG0035] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I had asthma as a kid, so my brain went there. He doesn't puff it every single day.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any medicine allergies?
[SEG0037] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Nothing.
[SEG0038] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No allergies.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Surgeries?
[SEG0040] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Nope, none.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tummy, pee, poop, all normal?
[SEG0042] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Tummy's fine, peeing normal. Appetite's shot though, he barely touched breakfast. Oh, and the parking meter outside is definitely going to nail us, just saying.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Who's he home with? Is he in school?
[SEG0044] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Both of us. Preschool three mornings. Half the class is out with this bug.
[SEG0045] person_1 (NURSE): Weight's 33 pounds today, whenever you get to dosing. He's been sitting pretty quiet for me.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thanks. Big breaths, Jonah. Throat's a little red, ears are clear, lungs are clear, no wheeze, no retractions. He's not working to breathe.
[SEG0047] person_5 (PATIENT): All done?
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Almost. Sorry, I lost the line I typed. The purple inhaler, two puffs, did you use a spacer?
[SEG0049] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yeah, with the spacer, two puffs at bedtime the last two nights. Not in the daytime.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): This looks like a viral upper respiratory infection to me. Fever, cough, exam isn't focal. I can't totally rule out early flu, but I'm not seeing pneumonia.
[SEG0051] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So no antibiotic?

[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not today. Use the children's Tylenol the right way, 160 milligrams, that's 5 mL, by mouth every six hours if the fever's bothering him. Use the syringe, not a kitchen spoon. Hold the Motrin so we're not doubling up on fuzzy doses.
[SEG0053] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): 5 mL, syringe. Got it.

[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): Push fluids, popsicles count. If he's breathing fast, or he gets limp and hard to wake, or the fever just isn't easing, come straight in. Purple inhaler, two puffs with the spacer, only if he's actually wheezing or working to breathe, not for an ordinary cough.
[SEG0055] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And if he's the same after the weekend?
[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): If he's not better in three days, come back and we'll recheck. Don't wait that long if he looks worse, obviously.
[SEG0057] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): What about preschool?
[SEG0058] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep him home while he's still feverish. Once the fever's been gone a full day, he can go back.
[SEG0059] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Syringe, fluids, home from school. Come on, bud.
[SEG0060] person_5 (PATIENT): I want grape.
